subject: Immediate: PrimeVault throughput and 5xx spike — emergency burst & exec approval
messages:
From: Ellen Harper <ellen.harper@primevault.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: support@primevault.com
Date: Thu, 1 Aug 2029 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: Repeated 5xx + high latency this morning — immediate help needed

Hi Logan / Naomi,

We started seeing a sharp rise in 5xx errors and token latency this morning (~08:45 PDT) across our inference endpoints. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% baseline to >8% and p95 latency doubled. Our support team attached a dump (/attachments/primevault_error_dump_20290801.log) and some request traces. This is impacting checkout flows for ~15% of our customers.

We've already retried and throttled a few noisiest clients on our side — but this looks like a capacity/backpressure problem on the Dedicated pool you provisioned for us (reserved capacity). Can you confirm:
- Are you seeing a saturated GPU pool for our reservations?
- Is there a mitigation path that doesn't require us to degrade model quality?

We need an ETA for mitigation and we expect compensation scope for the hours we were degraded. Victor from ops is on this thread.

Thanks — Ellen
Ellen Harper
Head of Platform Engineering, PrimeVault
ellen.harper@primevault.com | +1 415 555 0121

Attachment: primevault_error_dump_20290801.log (log)

Ellen — thanks for the heads up and for the traces. I’m escalating internally (ops + infra) and will own coordination with you until we stabilize. Immediate plan:

1) Olga & infra to confirm pool headroom and whether noisy neighbors are causing eviction.
2) Karthik to check model runtime metrics (KV cache pressure, batch queue lengths, kernel fallbacks).
3) We’ll propose short-term fallbacks (route a percentage of traffic to a hosted variant) while we free capacity on your Dedicated pool.

We’ll aim to send a triage update in 30 minutes and a fix plan within 90 minutes. If we need cross-customer burst capacity we’ll request exec sign-off (I’ve looped Vivek).

Logan Wright

log an.wright@redwood.ai | +1 510 555 3421

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Aug 2029 09:48:54 -07:00
Subject: RE: Repeated 5xx + high latency this morning — immediate help needed

Summary of quick triage (preliminary):
- Observed: Dedicated us-west pool node group PW-3 at 98–100% GPU utilization across N=12 nodes during 08:30–09:05. KV cache hit rate fell ~12%, queue depth spiked causing kernel fallback to slower FP32 path for a subset of models.
- Root cause hypothesis: simultaneous large prefix workloads from two heavy customers (PrimeVault + another tenant) plus a recent kernel library rollout that regressed batch coalescing for long-sequence requests.

Immediate mitigations I can push now (non-disruptive):
A) Re-route 25% of PrimeVault traffic to a compatible hosted model variant (identical weights quantized to 4-bit, slightly higher latency but steadier servicing).
B) Roll back the kernel library change on PW-3 (if accepted by infra) — this should restore batching behavior in ~12–15 minutes but may require a rolling restart per node.
C) Throttle/burst-shed low-priority background jobs for several hours.

If rollback + routing does not restore within 30m we'll need authorization for temporary burst nodes (cross-customer, pre-paid or emergency credit) or to swap PrimeVault to a different reserved pool with spare capacity — that request needs Vivek + finance sign-off for cost/credit adjustments.

I’ve attached a short snapshot and will push logs to the ticket.

— Karthik
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Attachment: pool-utilization-snapshot-0900.json (json)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Aug 2029 10:12:07 -07:00
Subject: RE: Repeated 5xx + high latency this morning — emergency capacity note

Triage update: Confirmed PW-3 node group saturated. Live metrics: GPU mem pressure and some eviction events; a noisy neighbor (unrelated tenant) triggered sustained KV cache churn. Rolling kernel rollback will require ~20% throughput hit briefly as we cycle nodes, but overall should restore batching efficiency.

Operations options (tradeoffs/estimates):
- Option 1 (fastest, lowest risk): Route 30% of PrimeVault live traffic to hosted variant (estimated 15–20 min to update routing and warm KV caches). No cost to PrimeVault beyond existing usage.
- Option 2 (short burst nodes): Provision 6 emergency burst GPUs in us-west for 4 hours. Estimated $Xk cost — needs exec approval (Vivek).
- Option 3 (rollback + node rolling restart): Begin rollback now, expected stabilization in 35–45 min; risk: transient 503s during node cycles.

Requesting Vivek’s sign-off for Option 2 if PrimeVault cannot accept hosted routing or transient restarts. Naomi — can you confirm whether PrimeVault accepts fallback routing? If not, we’ll ask for a temporary invoice amendment and burst credit.

— Olga
Site Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

From: logan_wright@redwood.ai
To: Ellen Harper <ellen.harper@primevault.com>, Victor Liang <victor.liang@fastops.io>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Aug 2029 10:28:41 -07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated 5xx + high latency this morning — emergency burst & exec approval

Ellen / Victor — quick update and asks so we can move fast:

What we’ll do now (agreed immediate steps):
1) Route 30% of your traffic to hosted-compatible model variant (non-destructive, will reduce load on Dedicated pool). We need your sign-off to enable this routing for 30–60 minutes while we stabilize.
2) Olga will start kernel rollback + rolling restart on PW-3 concurrently; expect stabilization within 40 minutes but brief 503 blips possible.
3) If neither step restores healthy p95/p99 within 30 minutes, we’ll provision 6 emergency burst GPUs (Option 2). Vivek — please authorize emergency burst spend up to $12,000 for the next 4 hours.

Ellen — can you confirm acceptance of (1) routing fallback? Naomi — please prepare a mutual action plan (attached draft) and draft an interim credit proposal (hours impacted) in case we need to offer compensation. I’ve added the DocuSign temp amendment link to the ticket for a rapid sign-off should we provision burst capacity and bill later.

We will do a follow-up at 11:00 PDT with full RC and remediation timeline. I’ll stay on this until resolved.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
log an.wright@redwood.ai

Logan — thanks. We accept routing 30% to the hosted variant as an immediate mitigation (please limit to non-auth-critical endpoints — we will route checkout to lowest-risk path). We also agree to the DocuSign amendment for temporary burst authorization if you need to spin nodes — Victor will coordinate signing.

A couple asks from our side:
- Timeline: can you confirm when the routing switch will be live and when you expect p95 to return to baseline?
- Compensation: we will require a credit for the window where checkout experiences degradation. Naomi — please include a credits framework in the MAP and include a line-item we can preliminarily agree to.

Appreciate the fast response.

— Ellen
Head of Platform Engineering, PrimeVault
